steps.title: Announcements — list, create, edit, delete, audience and scheduling
steps.goal: A leader with `announcements.create` writes an announcement at `/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/new` (title, body, audience group from the church's `audience_groups`, publish now or at a future date in the church's timezone, optional expiry, pinned, push on/off), sees it in the `/o/[orgSlug]/announcements` list with its state (Scheduled / Active / Expired) and a Push column that reads the `notifications` outbox row the DB trigger `app.on_content_publish` created ("Queued — delivered by the push dispatcher (step 3.6)"), edits it at `/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/[id]/edit` with `announcements.edit`, and deletes it with `announcements.delete` (the trigger cancels a queued push). Plain members see only published, unexpired announcements in their audience (RLS) and can expand a row to read the body. A no-op `afterContentPublish()` stub in `src/lib/push/after-publish.ts` marks the single call site that step 3.6a turns into the synchronous push dispatch. No uploads, no bulletins (3.5b), no push sending (3.6a), no cron (3.6b).

This is step 3.5a "Announcements — list, create, edit, delete, audience and scheduling" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. ## Goal
When you finish, a church leader holding `announcements.create` opens `/o/<slug>/announcements/new`, writes a title and body, picks the audience from the church's `audience_groups` (the six system groups first — All attendees, Members, Non-member attendees, Youth, Men, Women — then custom groups), chooses "Publish now" or a future date and time in the church's timezone, optionally sets an expiry, pins it, leaves "Send a push notification" on or turns it off, and saves. The row lands in `announcements`; the database trigger `app.on_content_publish` (step 1.3a) inserts one `notifications` row (`kind = 'announcement'`, `scheduled_for = publish_at`) when `push` is true — nothing in this step sends anything. The list at `/o/<slug>/announcements` shows every announcement with its state (Scheduled, Active, Expired), the audience name, pinned marker and a Push column that reads the outbox row: "Queued — delivered by the push dispatcher (step 3.6)". `announcements.edit` holders edit at `/o/<slug>/announcements/[id]/edit`; `announcements.delete` holders delete (the trigger `app.cancel_notifications_on_delete` cancels a still-queued push). Members without any `announcements.*` permission can open the list and see only what RLS lets them see (published, not expired, in their audience) with no controls, and every row expands to show the full body — the list is the only web surface for reading an announcement (PLAN §8 has no `/announcements/[id]`). Step 3.5b adds bulletins; step 3.6a replaces the stub `afterContentPublish()` with the real dispatcher; 3.6b adds the cron.

## Inputs / prior state
- Step 3.1 built the org shell and guards — reuse, never reshape: `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` (`requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext` with `org`, `membershipStatus`, `personId`, `householdId`, `permissions`, `isSuperAdmin`, `writable`; read the file for the exact org-id field name — 2.1a/3.1 disagree between `ctx.org.orgId` and `ctx.org.org_id`), `requirePerm(ctx, perm | perms[])` (array = any-of), `requireWritable(ctx)` (throws `organization_suspended`), `isWritable(ctx)`; `src/features/org/nav.ts` (`NAV_ITEMS` with a commented "3.5 Announcements/Bulletins" placeholder), `src/features/org/Dashboard.tsx` (the "Active announcements" card carries `TODO(3.5)`), `src/features/org/org-context.tsx`, `StatusBanner`; `src/lib/actions/result.ts` (`ActionResult<T>`), `src/lib/supabase/errors.ts` (`toActionError`), `src/lib/env.ts` (`publicEnv()`), `src/lib/supabase/server.ts` (user-scoped server client). Server Actions receive `orgSlug`, re-run `requireOrgMember` + `requirePerm`, validate with Zod, write with the USER client, return `ActionResult`.
- Steps 3.3a/3.3b (`src/features/sermons/*`) show the house style for list pages, forms (RHF + `zodResolver`, shadcn/ui, `sonner`), confirm dialogs and action tests. Copy the patterns, not the files — with ONE exception: 3.3a's web-side date helpers `src/features/sermons/dates.ts` (`zonedLocalToInstant(datetimeLocal, tz)` — `datetime-local` value → ISO instant in the org timezone, `formatInstantInZone(iso, tz)`, `formatDateOnly(isoDate)`, built on `@date-fns/tz` + `date-fns` or Intl) are promoted to `src/lib/dates.ts` in Build 2 and reused; do not write a second local→instant conversion.
- `@church/domain` (1.6a/1.6b): `schemas/announcement.ts` → `announcementSchema` (`title` 1–160, `body` ≤ 10000, `audience_group_id` nullable uuid, `document_id` nullable uuid, `publish_at` datetime — future allowed, `expires_at` nullable and `> publish_at`, `pinned` default false, `push` default true); `permissions.ts` (`PERMISSION_LABELS` only — permission checks in web code use `hasPerm(ctx, perm)` / `hasAnyPerm(ctx, perms)` from `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts`, NOT the `@church/domain` helpers of the same names that take a `PermissionKey[]`); `dates.ts` (`todayInZone`, `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` — Intl-only, no formatters, no `datetime-local` conversion); `errors.ts` (`toDomainError`, `errorMessageFor`); `audiences.ts` (`SYSTEM_AUDIENCE_GROUPS` — the six system group names/kinds in order).
- `@church/db` (1.7a, every helper takes the client first): `queries/announcements.ts` — `listAnnouncements(db, orgId, { includeScheduled, includeExpired })` ordered `pinned desc, publish_at desc`, `listFeed(db, orgId, { limit })` (the member query: `publish_at <= now()` and `expires_at is null or > now()`), `getAnnouncement(db, id)`, `insertAnnouncement(db, row)`, `updateAnnouncement(db, id, patch)`, `deleteAnnouncement(db, id)`, `listNotificationStatus(db, orgId)` (reads `notifications` by `(kind, ref_id)`); `queries/audience-groups.ts` — `listAudienceGroups(db, orgId)` (system rows first, then custom by name); `queries/settings.ts` — `getSettings(db, orgId)` (for `timezone`); `keys.ts` — `queryKeys.announcements.list(orgId, filters)`, `.announcements.feed(orgId)`. Read the real signatures first; extend additively (optional parameter, own test) only when unavoidable and record it in HANDOFF.
- Database facts that decide behaviour (read `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` sections (3), (5), (7), (8) for `announcements` and `notifications`): `announcements` columns `id, org_id, title, body, audience_group_id null, document_id null, publish_at default now(), expires_at, pinned, push default true, push_enqueued_at, created_by, updated_by`; RLS select = member ∧ published ∧ not expired ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)` OR any `announcements.*`; insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete`; `notifications` select = `announcements.*` managers. `app.user_in_group(null)` is true (an announcement with `audience_group_id = null` reaches everyone). Trigger `announcements_on_content_publish` (after insert or update) inserts a `notifications` row when `push` is true and `publish_at` is not null and no non-cancelled row exists for `(kind, ref_id)`, stamping `push_enqueued_at`; `announcements_cancel_notifications_on_delete` sets queued/claimed rows to `cancelled`.
- Founder decisions that apply: decision 4 — the permission mapping ships as the default (`announcements.create` creates, `.edit` edits, `.delete` deletes; nothing else unlocks these pages); decision 7 — "only `suspended` blocks writes; `past_due` = banner only" (`requireWritable` before every write; the banner is 3.1's). Orchestrator decision 7 fixes the ordering: "3.5 ships first: publishing inserts rows and the DB trigger enqueues `notifications` rows; the UI shows 'queued, delivered by the push dispatcher (step 3.6)'. 3.6 then adds `src/lib/push/*`, wires the publish Server Actions to call `dispatch()` synchronously after enqueue". Use that sentence as the Push column text.

## Build
1. **Push stub** `apps/web/src/lib/push/after-publish.ts`: `export type AfterPublishResult = { dispatched: false } | { dispatched: true; summary: unknown }` and `export async function afterContentPublish(_input: { orgId: string }): Promise<AfterPublishResult> { return { dispatched: false }; }` with a comment "Step 3.6a replaces this body with the synchronous push dispatch; keep the signature." Every Server Action below that publishes calls it once after a successful write and ignores the result. This file is the ONLY thing under `src/lib/push/` in this step.
2. **Timezone helpers — move, do not duplicate.** Read 3.3a's `src/features/sermons/dates.ts` (`zonedLocalToInstant(datetimeLocal, tz)`, `formatInstantInZone(iso, tz)`, `formatDateOnly(isoDate)`). Move the file to `apps/web/src/lib/dates.ts` (`git mv`; keep `src/features/sermons/dates.ts` as a one-line re-export so 3.3a/3.4a callers compile unchanged) and add there, additively and in the same style (`TZDate` from `@date-fns/tz` + `date-fns` `format` — both already `catalog:` dependencies of `apps/web` since 3.3a; add them as `catalog:` only if missing, never with a version), `instantToZonedLocal(iso, tz): string` returning `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` (the inverse of `zonedLocalToInstant`, minute precision, for prefilling the edit form). Every date/time in this step and in 3.5b goes through `src/lib/dates.ts`; `@church/domain` `dates.ts` stays Intl-only. Tests `src/lib/dates.test.ts` (move 3.3a's cases and extend): a New York summer and a winter instant round-trip through `zonedLocalToInstant` → `instantToZonedLocal`, the spring-forward gap hour (`02:30` on the DST day maps forward, does not throw), and `Europe/Berlin` vs `America/New_York` for the same input differ by the expected hours.
3. **State derivation** `src/features/announcements/announcement-state.ts`: `deriveAnnouncementState(row: { publish_at, expires_at }, now = new Date()): 'scheduled' | 'active' | 'expired'` and `ANNOUNCEMENT_STATE_LABELS`. `scheduled` = `publish_at > now`; `expired` = `expires_at` set and `<= now`; else `active`. Table test with the boundary instants.
4. **Schema wrapper** `src/features/announcements/form-schema.ts`: `announcementFormSchema` = the FORM shape (`title`, `body`, `audience_group_id` uuid — required in the UI, see 5 —, `publish_mode: 'now' | 'schedule'`, `publish_at_local` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`, required when `schedule`), `expires_at_local` optional, `pinned`, `push`) and `toAnnouncementInput(form, tz, now)` that produces the object `announcementSchema` accepts (`publish_at = now.toISOString()` for `now`; ISO via `zonedLocalToInstant` otherwise; `expires_at` null or ISO; `document_id: null`). Server Actions validate the RESULT with `announcementSchema` from `@church/domain` (single source of truth), never the form schema alone.
5. **AudienceGroupSelect** `src/features/announcements/AudienceGroupSelect.tsx` (client; shadcn `Select`): options = `listAudienceGroups` result passed from the server page — system groups first in `SYSTEM_AUDIENCE_GROUPS` order, a separator, then custom groups; default value = the system group with kind `everyone` ("All attendees"). The UI never writes `audience_group_id = null`: every announcement is stored against a group row (the `everyone` system group is the "no restriction" choice) so audience derivation and the fan-out in `srv_audience_user_ids(group, org)` follow one rule. Rows that already have `null` (created elsewhere) display as "Everyone". Helper text under the select: "Members are matched by the directory: sex, age and membership status decide Youth, Men, Women and Members (ages are set in Settings)". Custom groups are created in step 5.5 — show the separator only when custom rows exist.
6. **AnnouncementForm** `src/features/announcements/AnnouncementForm.tsx` (client; RHF + `zodResolver(announcementFormSchema)`): fields Title; Body (textarea, plain text, counter to 10000); Audience (component above); Publish — radio "Now" / "Schedule for", with a `datetime-local` input shown for "Schedule for", minimum = current minute in the org timezone, caption "Times are in <timezone>"; Expires (optional `datetime-local`, caption "Hidden from members after this time; the push is not affected"); Pinned (checkbox, "Pinned announcements stay at the top of the app feed"); Send a push notification (checkbox, default on, help "Members who installed the app and allow announcement notifications receive a push when this publishes. Editing later does not re-send."). Attach a document: render a disabled row "Available once Documents ship (step 5.4)" — `document_id` stays `null`; do NOT build a documents query. Submit label "Publish" / "Schedule" / "Save changes"; disabled while pending; field errors from `ActionResult.error.field`; `sonner` toast on success; when `!isWritable(ctx)` the whole form is read-only with 3.1's suspended explanation.
7. **Server Actions** `src/features/announcements/actions.ts` (`'use server'`), each: `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` → `requirePerm` → `requireWritable` → `getSettings` for `timezone` → `announcementSchema.parse(toAnnouncementInput(...))` → user client → `ActionResult`:
   - `createAnnouncementAction(orgSlug, form)` — `announcements.create`; `insertAnnouncement(db, { ...input, org_id, created_by: user id, updated_by: user id })`; `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/announcements')`, `afterContentPublish({ orgId })`, return `{ id, state }` so the client can toast "Published — push queued" / "Scheduled for <time>" / "Published — no push (turned off)".
   - `updateAnnouncementAction(orgSlug, id, form)` — `announcements.edit`; `getAnnouncement` first (404 → `not_found`); `updateAnnouncement(db, id, { ...input, updated_by })`; 0 rows updated → "You no longer have permission to edit announcements" (RLS refused); `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/announcements')` and `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/announcements/<id>/edit')`; then `afterContentPublish` (turning `push` on after publication enqueues a fresh row via the trigger — the only way an edit causes a push; say so in the form help). Changing `publish_at` of an already-queued push does NOT move the queued `scheduled_for` in this step; show the notice "Push already queued — the dispatcher checks the publish time before sending (step 3.6)" (3.6a rewrites this wording).
   - `deleteAnnouncementAction(orgSlug, id)` — `announcements.delete`; `deleteAnnouncement(db, id)`; 0 rows → permission message; `revalidatePath`.
   The Server Actions carry the `…Action` suffix because the `@church/db` queries `updateAnnouncement` / `deleteAnnouncement` own the plain names (same convention as 3.3b's `deleteSermonAction`); never alias imports to make same-named pairs compile.
   Map SQLSTATE 23514 (check violation, e.g. `expires_at` before `publish_at` if the DB has such a check) and 23503 (unknown `audience_group_id`) through `toDomainError` to field errors. Never import `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` here.
8. **Pages** (server components, `await params`): `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/page.tsx` — `requireOrgMember` (no `requirePerm`: members may read); compute `canCreate = hasPerm(ctx, 'announcements.create')`, `canEdit = hasPerm(ctx, 'announcements.edit')`, `canDelete = hasPerm(ctx, 'announcements.delete')` and `isManager = hasAnyPerm(ctx, ['announcements.create', 'announcements.edit', 'announcements.delete'])` with the helpers from `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts`; managers load `listAnnouncements(db, orgId, { includeScheduled: true, includeExpired: filter })` plus `listNotificationStatus(db, orgId)` and `listAudienceGroups`; non-managers load `listFeed(db, orgId, { limit: 100 })` (1.7a's member query; RLS remains the second line of defence) and get no status column and no filter. Search param `?show=active|scheduled|expired|all` for managers only (default `all`). `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/new/page.tsx` — `requirePerm(ctx, 'announcements.create')`, `AnnouncementForm` in create mode with the groups. `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/[id]/edit/page.tsx` — `requirePerm(ctx, 'announcements.edit')`, `getAnnouncement` (→ `notFound()`), form in edit mode prefilled via `instantToZonedLocal`, Delete button (only with `announcements.delete`) opening a confirm dialog that names the title and says "A queued push notification is cancelled; sent notifications cannot be recalled".
9. **AnnouncementsTable** `src/features/announcements/AnnouncementsTable.tsx`: columns Title (pinned icon + link to edit when allowed), Audience (group name; "Everyone" for null), Publishes/Published (`formatInstantInZone` from `src/lib/dates.ts`), Expires, State badge (`ANNOUNCEMENT_STATE_LABELS`), Push (managers only, `src/features/announcements/PushStatusBadge.tsx`: `push = false` → "Off"; no outbox row yet → "Not queued"; `queued` → "Queued — delivered by the push dispatcher (step 3.6)"; `claimed` → "Sending"; `sent` → "Sent <relative time>"; `failed` → "Failed"; `cancelled` → "Cancelled"; step 3.6a will extend this component with delivery counts and Retry — keep the status → label map in one exported function `pushStatusLabel(status, row)`), Actions (Edit / Delete). Every row expands (shadcn `Collapsible`, or a View button opening a `Dialog`) to show the full plain-text body (`whitespace-pre-wrap`), the audience name, publish and expiry times in the org zone and, for managers, the push status; the member view uses the same component, so a plain member can read an announcement on the web (there is no detail route). Empty states: "No announcements yet" with a Create button for `announcements.create`; the member view says "Nothing published for you right now".
10. **Nav and dashboard**: in `src/features/org/nav.ts` replace the commented 3.5 placeholder with `{ href: 'announcements', label: 'Announcements', icon: …, requires: undefined }` (visible to every member — the page itself decides what it shows); leave the Bulletins placeholder commented for 3.5b. In `src/features/org/Dashboard.tsx` turn the "Active announcements" count into a link to `/o/<slug>/announcements` and remove its `TODO(3.5)`; leave the bulletin card's `TODO(3.5)` for 3.5b.
11. **Tests** (2.1a Vitest harness, jsdom): `src/lib/dates.test.ts` (moved from 3.3a and extended), `announcement-state.test.ts`, `form-schema.test.ts` (`now` mode uses the injected clock; `schedule` converts in the org zone; `expires_at` before `publish_at` fails on `expires_at`), `actions.test.ts` with mocked `@church/db` modules and guards (create without `announcements.create` → `permission_denied`; update without `announcements.edit` → `permission_denied`; delete without `announcements.delete` → `permission_denied`; suspended org → `organization_suspended`; 0 rows updated → the permission message; `afterContentPublish` called exactly once on create and update, never on delete), `AnnouncementsTable.test.tsx` (member view has no Push column; manager view renders the queued text; expanding a row renders the body text), `nav.test.ts` update (Announcements visible with no permissions). If `apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` exists (3.7 may not have created it yet), add: signed-out `/o/unknown/announcements` → `/login?next=…`.
12. **Copy**: every user-facing string in English, sentence case, no jargon; the Push column text is verbatim from orchestrator decision 7.

## Constraints
- Web never holds elevated keys: no `service.ts` import anywhere in `src/features/announcements/`; all reads and writes go through the user client and `@church/db`. No raw `supabase.from(...)` in components or actions — add helpers to `packages/db` additively (with tests) if one is missing and record it in HANDOFF.
- Do not touch `supabase/` (no migrations; `9999_init.sql` may be frozen — check the HANDOFF ledger), `apps/web/vercel.json`, `proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts`, CSP, the share/users features, `/admin`, or the sermons feature beyond the `dates.ts` move + re-export of Build 2. Do not build bulletins (3.5b), uploads, documents (5.4), custom groups (5.5), push sending (3.6a) or the cron (3.6b), or a mobile feed.
- Announcement body is plain text in Phase 1 — no markdown renderer, no HTML.
- Pins: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3, Zod 4.5, date-fns 4.4 + `@date-fns/tz` from the catalog, shadcn/ui components from `src/components/ui/*` (generate missing ones with the project's shadcn setup, do not hand-write). No new dependencies beyond those. No model names in commits.
- Never `supabase db push` or `supabase db reset`.

- `pnpm --filter web build` → succeeds; the route list shows `/o/[orgSlug]/announcements`, `/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/new`, `/o/[orgSlug]/announcements/[id]/edit`.

Without access to the hosted project, write this script into `session_log.md` for the founder.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: State checklist — the web line is one combined entry ("Web: auth, super admin, org admin (users/permissions, settings, sermons, share links, announcements, bulletins, push, cron)"); mark its `announcements` sub-item the way steps 3.1–3.4 marked theirs (e.g. `announcements ✔ (3.5a)` inside the parentheses, or per-feature checkboxes if an earlier step already split the line) — do not invent a new item; feature table row "Announcements + push" → Web UI "create/edit/delete/schedule done (3.5a); push dispatch 3.6a"; "Decisions" — "UI always stores an `audience_group_id` (the `everyone` system group means no restriction); `document_id` stays null until step 5.4; `afterContentPublish()` in `src/lib/push/after-publish.ts` is the single dispatch call site for 3.6a"; "Deviations from plan" — `src/features/sermons/dates.ts` promoted to `src/lib/dates.ts` (+ `instantToZonedLocal`), the `…Action` naming, anything else you changed (additive `@church/db` helpers, a differing column name); a note for 3.5b ("reuse `PushStatusBadge`/`pushStatusLabel`, `src/lib/dates.ts` `formatInstantInZone`, and the `…Action` naming") and for 3.6a ("replace the stub body; extend `pushStatusLabel` with deliveries and Retry; rewrite the two 'step 3.6' strings").
- Tick step 3.5a in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(web): announcements — list, create, edit, delete, audience and scheduling`; push `main`.
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong (for example the trigger behaves differently from the description above), do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

steps.title: Bulletins — This Sunday / Quarter presets, PDF/JPG/PNG upload, list, open, delete
steps.goal: A leader with `bulletins.upload` opens `/o/[orgSlug]/bulletins`, picks "This Sunday", "Quarter" or a custom date range (the presets compute `starts_on`/`ends_on` in the church's timezone), chooses a PDF, JPG or PNG up to 25 MiB and uploads it with the generic resumable uploader from step 3.3b along the exact-path flow (insert row with `publish_at = null` → tus upload to `{org_id}/bulletins/{bulletin_id}/{uuid}.{ext}` → finalize and publish). The list shows every bulletin with its date range, a "Current" badge for the one covering today, Open/Download through 1-hour signed URLs, a Push column for announcement managers (the DB trigger enqueues a `bulletin` notification when `push_on_bulletin` is on — founder decision 6; RLS lets only `announcements.*` holders read the outbox, so a `bulletins.upload`-only leader sees a hint instead) and Delete (the trigger enqueues the object into `storage_deletions`). Incomplete uploads can be resumed or discarded. Members see published bulletins read-only. No push sending (3.6a), no cron (3.6b).

## Goal
When you finish, `GET /api/cron/tick` exists: Vercel calls it every five minutes with `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` (Pro cron `*/5 * * * *` from `apps/web/vercel.json`, shipped in 1.1) and it runs the idempotent maintenance chain in this exact order — enqueue due notifications → dispatch (3.6a's `dispatchQueued`) → Expo receipts (3.6a's `processReceipts`) → drain `storage_deletions` → sweep orphan storage objects older than 24 h → `srv_housekeeping()` → `srv_process_account_deletions()` — and answers with a JSON phase report. Future-dated announcements, bulletins deleted on the web, cancelled churches' files, expired invitations, stale claims and account-deletion requests are all handled by this one route. Everything is idempotent under overlapping runs, the route is excluded from the auth proxy, and `docs/ENV.md` explains `CRON_SECRET`, the Hobby fallback and how to trigger the tick by hand. The founder verifies with `curl` and the Vercel Cron Jobs page.

## Inputs / prior state
- 3.6a: `src/lib/push/dispatch.ts` (`dispatchQueued(svc, { transport, limit, now, deadlineMs })` → `DispatchSummary`), `src/lib/push/receipts.ts` (`processReceipts(svc, { transport, olderThanMinutes, limit, now })`), `src/lib/push/expo.ts` (`createExpoTransport({ accessToken })`, `PushTransport`), `serverEnv().expoAccessToken`, the `receipt_status` vocabulary `null | ok | error | unknown`. - 2.1a: `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` → `createServiceSupabase()` (branded `ServiceDbClient`), `src/lib/env.ts` (`serverEnv()` already exposes `cronSecret` from `CRON_SECRET` — 2.1a listed it; if it is missing add it additively as `string | undefined`, never throwing), `proxy.ts` whose `config.matcher` already excludes `/api/cron/tick` (`src/lib/auth/paths.ts` has the predicate and a test) — verify, do not widen anything else. 1.1: `apps/web/vercel.json` with `{"crons": [{"path": "/api/cron/tick", "schedule": "*/5 * * * *"}]}` — founder decision 10: Vercel Pro → `*/5` allowed; Hobby fallback `0 12 * * *` documented in `docs/ENV.md`. Verify, do not rewrite. `apps/web/.env.example` (2.1a) lists `CRON_SECRET`.
- `@church/db` (1.7a; service-only helpers take `ServiceDbClient`): `rpc.ts` — `srvEnqueueDueNotifications(svc)` → count, `srvHousekeeping(svc)` → jsonb counts, `srvProcessAccountDeletions(svc)` → count (read the file: argument keys equal the SQL parameter names); `queries/storage.ts` — `listStorageDeletions(svc, limit)`, `markStorageDeletionDone(svc, id)`, `markStorageDeletionFailed(svc, id, error)` (`attempts + 1`, `last_error`), `listObjects(svc, bucket, prefix, { limit = 1000, offset = 0 })` wrapping `svc.storage.from(bucket).list(prefix, …)`, `enqueueStorageDeletion(svc, { bucket_id, object_name, is_prefix })`, and `listReferencedPaths(svc, bucket)` returning every `storage_path` / `photo_path` / `logo_path` the tables hold for that bucket (`sermons`, `bulletins`, `documents`, `households` + `persons`, `organization_settings`) — 1.7a wrote it precisely for this step's orphan sweep; `queries/organizations.ts` — `listOrganizations` (super-admin shape, joins settings and billing; NOT what the sweep needs — see Build 3).

- Database semantics you rely on (1.3b; read the function bodies in `9999_init.sql`): `srv_enqueue_due_notifications()` inserts missing `notifications` rows for publish-worthy content (same predicates as `app.on_content_publish`, restricted to `publish_at`/`opens_at <= now()`) and returns the count; `srv_housekeeping()` prunes `private.rate_limits`, expires invitations, deletes upload-kind draft sermons older than 7 days without an object, re-queues `claimed` notifications older than 10 minutes without `sent_at`, flips `trial → past_due` after `trial_ends_at`, and purges `cancelled` orgs older than 30 days by enqueueing prefix deletions (`is_prefix = true`, `object_name = '<org_id>/'`) for the five buckets; `srv_process_account_deletions()` deletes the auth users of pending requests and stamps `processed_at`. `storage.objects` has no update/delete policy for `authenticated` — deletion happens only here, with the service role.

## Build
1. **Cron route** `apps/web/app/api/cron/tick/route.ts`: `export const runtime = 'nodejs'; export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'; export const maxDuration = 60;` `GET(req: Request)`: read `serverEnv().cronSecret`; unset → 503 `{ error: 'cron_not_configured' }` (log once per process); compare the `Authorization` header to `Bearer <secret>` with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers → 401 `{ error: 'unauthorized' }` otherwise (Vercel sends this header automatically when the `CRON_SECRET` environment variable exists — document). Then `runTick(createServiceSupabase(), { transport: createExpoTransport({ accessToken: serverEnv().expoAccessToken }), deadlineMs: 50_000 })` and respond with JSON `{ ok, startedAt, durationMs, phases }`; HTTP 200 when every phase succeeded, 500 when any phase threw (all phases still run — Vercel's cron log then shows the failure). Also `export const POST = GET` so a manual trigger from the Vercel dashboard works. Never read the secret from the query string.
2. **Tick phases** `apps/web/src/lib/cron/tick.ts` — `runTick(svc, { transport, now = () => new Date(), deadlineMs })` runs the phases in this exact order, each wrapped in `phase(name, fn)` that records `{ ok, ms, result | error }` and never stops the chain: (1) `enqueue` → `srvEnqueueDueNotifications(svc)`; (2) `dispatch` → `dispatchQueued(svc, { transport, limit: 200, deadlineMs: 25_000, now })`; (3) `receipts` → `processReceipts(svc, { transport, now })`; (4) `storageDeletions` → `drainStorageDeletions(svc, { limit: 100 })`; (5) `orphanSweep` → `sweepOrphans(svc, { now })`; (6) `housekeeping` → `srvHousekeeping(svc)`; (7) `accountDeletions` → `srvProcessAccountDeletions(svc)`. Stop starting new phases when `deadlineMs` is exhausted and report the skipped ones as `{ ok: false, error: 'deadline' }`. Header comment on idempotency: overlapping ticks are safe because claiming uses `skip locked`, deletions are idempotent (not-found counts as done), receipts are keyed by ticket, the sweep only enqueues, and the `srv_*` functions are re-runnable.
3. **Storage drain** `src/lib/cron/storage-deletions.ts` — `drainStorageDeletions(svc, { limit })`: `listStorageDeletions(svc, limit)` → for `is_prefix = false` remove the single object (`removeObjects(svc, bucket, [name])` — additive in `queries/storage.ts` wrapping `svc.storage.from(bucket).remove(names)`; "object not found" counts as done) → `markStorageDeletionDone`; for `is_prefix = true` list up to 1000 objects under the prefix (`listObjects`; recurse one level for folder entries — Storage lists folders as entries without `id`), remove them, and mark done only when the listing came back empty (large prefixes finish over several ticks); failures → `markStorageDeletionFailed` (`attempts + 1`, `last_error`); rows with `attempts >= 10` are skipped and reported. Returns `{ processed, done, failed, skipped, objectsRemoved }`.
4. **Orphan sweep** `src/lib/cron/orphan-sweep.ts` — `sweepOrphans(svc, { now, bucket? })`: one bucket per tick, rotating over `['sermon-media', 'bulletins', 'documents', 'directory-photos', 'org-assets']` by `Math.floor(now().getTime() / 300_000) % 5` (5-minute epochs — with the Hobby fallback `0 12 * * *` a minute-based rotation would sweep only the first bucket forever); `bucket` overrides the rotation for tests. List objects per org prefix: `listOrganizationIds(svc): Promise<string[]>` (additive in `queries/organizations.ts` — `select id from organizations`; `listOrganizations` joins settings and billing and is not for this) → for each org `listObjects(svc, bucket, '<org_id>/', …)` recursing into the folder entries, capping the total at 1000 objects per tick (continue with the next org on the next tick — keep it stateless: cap and move on); keep objects with `created_at < now - 24 h`; `listReferencedPaths(svc, bucket)` → a `Set` of referenced names (extend it additively with an optional `{ names }` filter only if the full list proves too large; never add a second helper for the same job); every listed name not in the set → `enqueueStorageDeletion(svc, { bucket_id, object_name, is_prefix: false, org_id })` — extend `enqueueStorageDeletion` additively with an optional `org_id` (the object's first path segment) since 1.7a's signature lacks it and the 1.2 table has the column; record it in HANDOFF. The sweep never removes anything itself: the drain deletes on the next tick — two-phase, so a sweep bug can be caught in the table before anything is destroyed. Returns `{ bucket, listed, orphansEnqueued }`.
5. **Docs**: `docs/ENV.md` — the `CRON_SECRET` row (how Vercel injects the header; generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`; Pro `*/5 * * * *`, Hobby `0 12 * * *` fallback; set it in Vercel for Production and Preview) and a "Push & maintenance job" section: what the tick does in order, the retry rules (≤ 5 attempts, re-queue of stale claims after 10 min by `srv_housekeeping`), the two-phase orphan sweep and its bucket rotation, the storage drain's 10-attempt cap, how to trigger manually (`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET" https://<VERCEL_URL>/api/cron/tick`), the response shape, and that a Free-plan Supabase project paused after 7 idle days makes every phase fail until restored. Ensure `apps/web/.env.example` contains `CRON_SECRET=` with the comment `# openssl rand -hex 32` (add if missing). `README.md`: one line pointing to that section. If 3.5b's Bulletins paragraph left the question open, state whether incomplete bulletin rows are purged by `srv_housekeeping` (read its body) or persist until discarded.
6. **Tests** (Vitest; `vi.mock` the `@church/db` modules and 3.6a's `dispatchQueued` / `processReceipts`; never call the network):
